key_insight: A transformer-based inpainting model can plausibly and consistently complete missing textures from very sparse multi-camera captures, enabling high-quality, low-latency 3D streaming with fewer viewpoints.
problem_solved: Fills holes and incomplete surfaces that arise when real-time 3D streaming must operate with a limited number of camera views; replaces ad-hoc heuristics that produce visual inconsistencies and artifacts.
method: Project multi-camera captures into a shared surface/texture space (e.g., UV or target view) and detect missing regions.
Apply a specialized transformer inpainting network that uses cross-view and spatial attention to synthesize coherent texture for gaps while preserving geometric cues.
Design and optimize the model and pipeline for streaming constraints (low latency, compact representations, temporal consistency losses) so it runs in real time on practical hardware.
impact: Improves visual fidelity and consistency in real-time 3D/AR/VR streaming systems while reducing the number of required cameras and bandwidth; practical for ML engineers building immersive systems under strict latency and capture constraints.

paper_title: Transformer-Based Inpainting for Real-Time 3D Streaming in Sparse Multi-Camera Setups
paper_authors: Leif Van Holland, Domenic Zingsheim, Mana Takhsha, Hannah Dröge, Patrick Stotko
